title: Temporary augmentation and debounce strategy for dedicated capacity shortfalls
creator: Priya Shah
summary: During a production incident on 2026-02-28 we observed sustained capacity shortfalls in multiple Dedicated pools. This ticket captures the temporary augmentation and debounce (autoscaler tuning) strategy used during the incident, the root cause analysis, and an actionable postmortem with owners and deadlines.
timeline:
2026-02-28 09:12 UTC: Alerts triggered (p95 latency > 2.5s, error rate increase).
2026-02-28 09:20 UTC: Ops increased reserved burst for two affected pools by +40% (manual scale).
2026-02-28 09:45 UTC: Rolling revert of autoscaler debounce config (reverted change from 2026-02-25).
2026-02-28 10:15 UTC: Traffic rebalanced; latency returned to normal range.
2026-03-01 15:00 UTC: Root cause initial hypothesis captured.
2026-03-05 11:30 UTC: Runtime patch landed (PR #1284) to reduce bootstrap time.
2026-03-09 16:00 UTC: Autoscaler safety gates and synthetic load test added to CI smoke suite.
root_cause: Two concurrent regressions combined to underprovision capacity: (1) a change in autoscaler debounce settings (scaleUp delay increased from 8s to 60s) deployed 2026-02-25 which made the autoscaler slow to react to spikes; (2) a runtime change in v1.20 that increased worker process bootstrap time by ~45s for certain model artifacts due to deferred kernel loading. The slow bootstrap pushed effective time-to-ready past the autoscaler's stabilization window, so the autoscaler did not create enough workers fast enough. Reduced burst policy (config change to limit burst to 10%) prevented manual autoscaling from absorbing the demand quickly.
mitigation_summary: We performed a three-step mitigation: 1) manual temporary augmentation: increase reserved burst for affected Dedicated pools by +40% and added 2 extra prewarmed nodes; 2) revert autoscaler debounce config to prior values (scaleUp delay 8s) to allow faster reaction; 3) deploy runtime patch reducing bootstrap time. Combined actions restored capacity and normalized latency within ~90 minutes.
rollback_and_temp_measures:
- Reverted autoscaler debounce commit (revert: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/ae92f3)
- Manually increased pool_reserved_burst_pct to 50% for pools: eu-west-1-dedicated-3, us-east-1-dedicated-7
- Created a short-lived emergency job to prewarm 10 workers per pool for 4 hours
- Added a throttle rule to prevent simultaneous draining of >20% of nodes in a pool during deploys
postmortem_findings:
- Root cause is interaction between autoscaler tuning and runtime startup regression, not a single failing metric.
- Monitoring gaps: we did not have an alert for 'time_to_ready' (worker bootstrap time) or for aggregate 'scale_lag' (demand vs ready workers).
- CI did not catch the runtime bootstrap regression because our smoke tests used small model artifacts; real customer model artifacts have different kernel paths.
- Our runbook allowed manual scale but lacked an explicit 'augment then revert' checklist with owners.
